name: Janco Electronics Inc.
old_description: Janco Electronics is a People-First Contract Assembly Company
about:
Janco Electronics Inc. operates from Rollinsford, New Hampshire. The business traces its roots to 1958 when brothers Lewis, George, and Paul Janetos founded the Janco Company, initially introducing plastic materials for Green Bay Packers shoulder pads. In 1966 the company expanded into electronics manufacturing, and in 1985 Lewis E. Janetos incorporated Janco Electronics as a separate entity. The founder led the company until 2001, when his son Rollins Janetos assumed the presidency, keeping the firm family-owned.

The company provides full-service electronics contract manufacturing and assembly. Core processes include surface‑mount pick‑and‑place, through‑hole technology, fine‑pitch BGA placement and rework, electro‑mechanical system integration, flex‑circuit assembly, conformal coating, and a range of test services such as flying‑probe, in‑circuit, functional, RF/microwave, and 2D X‑ray with 3D capability. Additional offerings cover new‑product introduction (NPI), design‑for‑manufacturability (DFM), cable‑assembly prototyping, supply‑chain management, turnkey assembly, just‑in‑time (JIT) manufacturing, and counterfeit‑component mitigation. A modern facility at 50 Goodwin Road houses the equipment and certified technicians; headcount is not publicly disclosed. Production spans prototype through high‑volume runs.

Janco serves customers in defense, medical (including medical‑device manufacturing), commercial, industrial, automotive, aerospace, and telecommunications/RF sectors. Its client base consists primarily of original‑equipment manufacturers requiring high‑reliability electronic assemblies and box‑build integration.

The company states that its founding philosophy — articulated by Lewis E. Janetos — centers on valuing people as the primary resource for continuous improvement and innovation. Quality is underscored by ISO 13485:2016 certification, adherence to IPC‑A‑610 and J‑STD‑001 standards, and lean‑manufacturing practices.
